1.explanation: All of the Verilog-specific highlighting rules live in src/languages/verilog.js. In that file, the patterns for backtick constructs (both for directives such as `define and macro uses like `CONSTANT) currently use an end-of-line terminator, causing everything after the backtick to be scoped as meta. To correct the issue, you must refine those regex rules in verilog.js so that only the identifier immediately following the backtick is marked as meta/keyword, leaving subsequent comments or code to their proper scopes.
1.bug_scenario: In Verilog mode, any backtick (`` ` ``) sequence—whether a preprocessor directive like `` `define`` or a macro reference like `` `CONSTANT``—is being lexed as a single “meta” token extending all the way to the end of the line. As a result, normal comments (// …) or ordinary code after the backtick-driven token loses its proper highlighting and is swallowed into the meta scope.

2.explanation: The file src/languages/verilog.js contains the grammar definition for Verilog in highlight.js. In it there is a rule that matches a backtick (`) and then runs to the end of line as a single meta token. That is exactly the rule mis‐scoping `define and backtick identifiers. Editing or refining this rule (for example, restricting its end or matching only specific directive keywords) will correct the incorrect meta highlighting.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting Verilog code, the built‐in Verilog grammar file (verilog.js) treats every backquote (`) as the start of a “meta” span that runs to end of line. That causes backquote‐defines (e.g. `define) and backtick‐references (e.g. `CONSTANT) to be colored as meta all the way to the // comment, rather than recognizing the keyword, the identifier, the comment, etc., as separate tokens.
